$comment: The model tiers: which model and reasoning effort each kind of work runs on, per provider, and what each model costs. One place for all of it: the installer reads it to write the AGENTS.md tier table and each agent's model for every targeted tool, lint checks the agents against it, and the usage report prices recorded sessions with it. An install copies it to .agents/models.json; a project adapts it in .agents/sdlc.config.json under `models` (its own prices, another model for a tier), never here. Prices are USD per million tokens at the standard tier, for prompts up to the `long.above` threshold where one is given; `cacheWrite` is the 5-minute cache write and `cacheWrite1h` the 1-hour one (Claude Code writes the main conversation's cache for an hour and a subagent's for five minutes). Check them against each provider's `source` when `asOf` gets old.

frontier.use: critical plans and reviews, bugs that survived two attempts

medium.use: building to a plan, tests, routine fixes

low.use: search, check output, docs, mechanical edits

orchestrator.$comment: The session itself: the agent the developer talks to. It runs on the strongest model the developer's tool and account have — the frontier tier, else high — and spends it on judgement, handing every step bigger than a subagent's cold start to the agent of its tier. A provider's `session` is the model name that resolves to that per account (Claude Code's `best`: Fable where the account has it, Opus otherwise); the installer sets it as Claude Code's starting model unless the project chose one.
orchestrator.use: your own session: the brief, the plan's decisions, routing each step, checking what comes back

families.$comment: Older or unlisted models of a family belong to its tier, so a session recorded on last year's models is still grouped and priced.
